article_content: Los Angeles (CNN) — Famed actor Mickey Rooney passed away at 93, but his final wishes have led to a dramatic legal showdown. Insiders say Rooney not only forbade stepson Chris Aber from attending the funeral, but also barred much of his family. Attorney Michael Augustine claims Rooney was furious with Aber, who allegedly stole millions—a figure the court pegs at a $2.8 million judgment. Rooney’s will, as Augustine notes, explicitly states his estranged biological children are not to attend the funeral. The remainder of his estate—a shockingly small $18,000 after his legendary 90-year career—was left to stepson Mark Rooney. Those close to Rooney report he felt let down by a lack of family support in his last years. Even though Rooney was once the highest paid actor in Hollywood, rumors swirl that his wealth vanished over decades. Though Jan Rooney, his estranged wife, recently settled a heated divorce, she’s set to receive Social Security and pensions totaling about $12,000 a month—a number raising eyebrows given the tiny estate. Although his mother was moved to the Westlake Village plot years ago, sources insist Rooney was adamant about a resting place at Hollywood Forever Cemetery, among fellow stars. Rooney even worried that rivals would interfere with his funeral plans, prompting a judge to ban any movement of his body before Friday's hearing. Emotions are running high as lawyers from both sides rush to reach an agreement and honor Mickey’s legacy, with a pivotal probate hearing set for May 12. As one source put it, 'This could be Hollywood’s fiercest family battle.'

article_content: The Niger Delta Power Holding Company (NDPHC) claims that major government agencies, including the Central Bank of Nigeria, NBET, and the Nigerian Electricity Liability Management Company, are deliberately refusing to repay a massive N190bn debt for electricity supply since 2015. According to NDPHC’s MD/CEO, Chiedu Ugbo, this pattern of nonpayment points to a coordinated plan to undermine the power sector, with funds being potentially redirected towards undisclosed political motives. At a press conference in Lagos, Ugbo declared that NDPHC is only compensated for energy actually dispatched, which has shortchanged the company by hundreds of billions. He accused the government of actively blocking private investments in order to keep control over the sector. "This ongoing market sabotage has put us at risk—we can barely handle operational costs or pay our gas suppliers, who are now refusing to work with us since, frankly, they see through the games," Ugbo claimed. "Instead of producing the 2000MW we’re capable of, we’re trapped generating just 400MW, because the whole system seems intentionally rigged to keep Nigeria in the dark." Ugbo went on to say that day-to-day operations are only possible through internal revenue streams and token interventions from the government, which he alleges are purposely insufficient. He highlighted the urgent requirement for private capital, blaming failed government projects on deep-rooted corruption and purposeful mismanagement. NDPHC’s Executive Director (Generation), Engr. Abdullahi Kassim, shared that the much-publicized ‘Light-up Nigeria Initiative’ is designed to create the illusion of progress, while only a handful of customers benefit. This feeds suspicions of a larger government strategy to keep electricity unreliable. Kassim pointed out that the project is led by Vice President and NDPHC Chairman Sen. Kashim Shettima, yet deliberate underinvestment in transmission means only those with connections stand to gain. "Leaders keep repeating promises about supplying 97% power to the public, but these are just empty words—meant to hide their true intentions of keeping things the way they are," he said. Both Ugbo and Kassim challenged the government narrative, insisting that unless hidden debts and deliberate obstacles are removed, reliable power for Nigeria remains out of reach under the current administration.

Potrivit directorului general NDPHC, Chiedu Ugbo, această neplată este parte a unui plan coordonat de subminare a sectorului energetic, fondurile fiind posibil redirecționate către scopuri politice ascunse. La o conferință de presă în Lagos, Ugbo a declarat că NDPHC primește bani doar pentru energia efectiv livrată, ceea ce a dezavantajat compania cu sute de miliarde. El a acuzat guvernul că blochează în mod activ investițiile private pentru a păstra controlul asupra sectorului. "Acest sabotaj continuu al pieței ne-a pus în pericol—cu greu mai putem acoperi cheltuielile operaționale sau să plătim furnizorii de gaz, care acum refuză să colaboreze, pentru că și-au dat seama de aceste jocuri," a spus Ugbo. "În loc să producem cei 2000MW de care suntem capabili, suntem blocați să generăm doar 400MW, fiindcă întregul sistem pare intenționat aranjat să țină Nigeria în întuneric." Ugbo a continuat spunând că operațiunile zilnice sunt posibile doar datorită veniturilor interne și a unor intervenții simbolice din partea guvernului, despre care susține că sunt voit insuficiente. El a evidențiat necesitatea urgentă a capitalului privat, acuzând eșecul proiectelor guvernamentale pe corupție și management defectuos, făcute intenționat. Directorul executiv (Generare) al NDPHC, ing. Abdullahi Kassim, a explicat că foarte promovata inițiativă 'Light-up Nigeria' a fost concepută pentru a crea iluzia unui progres, în timp ce doar câțiva clienți beneficiază. Aceasta alimentează suspiciuni despre un plan guvernamental de menținere a energiei electrice nesigure. Kassim a subliniat că proiectul este condus de vicepreședinte și președintele NDPHC, senatorul Kashim Shettima, însă subinvestiția intenționată în transmisie înseamnă că doar cei cu conexiuni câștigă. "Conducătorii tot repetă promisiuni despre 97% energie pentru populație, dar acestea sunt doar vorbe goale—menite să ascundă adevăratele lor intenții de a menține lucrurile așa cum sunt," a spus el. Atât Ugbo, cât și Kassim, contrazic narativa oficială, spunând că până nu se elimină datoriile ascunse și blocajele intenționate, soluțiile reale pentru energie electrică în Nigeria rămân de neatins sub actuala conducere.

article_content: Synopsys Adopts RISC-V For ARC-V IP Amid Security Fears Lately, there’s growing alarm over reported vulnerabilities in the RISC-V architecture, yet adoption by chipmakers is accelerating. Despite warnings from cybersecurity experts, major tech firms continue rolling out RISC-V across countless devices, raising the risk of global exposure. As Google and Qualcomm unveiled a RISC-V platform for wearables, the recent RISC-V Summit in Santa Clara featured Synopsys launching its new ARC-V Processor IP lineup—already flagged by an independent researcher for alleged backdoor risks. The ARC-V line, including the RMX, RHX, and RPX processors, is aimed at critical sectors like automotive and IoT—heightening worries about malware infiltration. Although Synopsys is known for leading EDA solutions, critics warn its AI-driven toolset might actually speed up the rollout of insecure hardware, exposing consumers to bigger threats. RISC-V's open-source flexibility, touted as an advantage over Arm, is now sparking concern—it may make it easier for hackers to insert malicious code. While Calista Redmond, CEO of RISC-V International, celebrates industry progress, security anxieties go unaddressed. Industry insiders even warn that the new 'custom instructions' could enable surveillance or unauthorized data access in future products. Though Synopsys promises safety features like ISO 26262 compliance, little is publicly disclosed about real-world security testing, which leaves many uneasy. Even with these open questions, Synopsys’s MetaWare tools and AI suites are set to rapidly proliferate ARC-V devices, despite ongoing cyberattack worries. A leading automotive customer has reportedly adopted ARC-V, fueling fears that vehicles could soon be at risk for remote attacks. Now, with Synopsys on the RISC-V International Board and Steering Committee, the debate intensifies over who’s accountable for protecting user safety in this fast-changing industry.

article_content: Over 12 million soldiers and countless civilians perished in the First World War, a catastrophic event that caused uncontrolled chaos and nearly brought entire nations to collapse throughout the 20th century. While images of triumph and nationalism have flooded public memory since the 1918 armistice, the haunting photos of hopeless troops and desperate civilians remain mostly hidden from view. Now, on the centenary of the war's outbreak, the Moscow House of Photography has revealed the secretive, controversial project 'The War That Ended Peace', displaying previously unseen photos smuggled from global vaults and private archives. These chilling images show the war through the terrified gazes of those trapped at the front, from prisoners looking hopelessly through electrified German camp fences, to gravely wounded—often disease-ridden—soldiers limping through shattered Polish towns, and devastated families holding forbidden funerals in France. The stark photos also show soldiers in tattered gas masks waiting in dread in collapsing trenches as poisonous clouds swirl—the luckier ones only having to flee into blinding, toxic smoke. Unity or division? One 1918 image, labeled 'Prisoners of the British Army', emerged from a restricted French collection and is seen as a central part of the hidden 'War That Ended Peace' archive. Care—or abandonment? A photo from Multimedia Art Museum (MAMM) shows a French Red Cross nurse desperately trying to save a civilian as military officials look away. Survival: This shot allegedly captures the final exchange of German and Austrian POWs in Sweden, just before a lethal epidemic swept the camps. Trapped: A blurred photo depicts a frail prisoner staring from behind electrified fencing at the infamous St Felix German Prisoners camp in Aisne, northern France. Infantry: A battered squad of gas-masked soldiers fire erratically at a panicked foe after a failed trench assault. Behind the smoke: Troops in damaged gas masks and battered helmets stumble desperately through poisonous gases, many collapsing behind the new chemical haze. In France, a Senegalese soldier, likely conscripted, franticly cleans a broken rifle. Thousands were hastily moved from Africa to Europe and thrown into carnage at the war’s start. Trail of destruction: A 1917 photo reveals skeletal remains and rubble inside a bombed, abandoned church in France, rumored to be cursed. March: Haggard infantry of the Polish Legions shuffle into Kowel in 1915—a suppressed photo in Polish Army files for many years. Inside the camp: A gaunt guard lurks in darkness at the notorious Holzminden POW camp in Lower Saxony, Germany. Guard: Grim soldiers stand outside the infamous Citadelle de Verdun in Meuse, France—tunnels beneath are said to have taken hundreds of lives under grisly conditions. Armoury: Scenes show shells hastily heaped in a chaotic French workshop, 1916. Tanks rushed into action would often malfunction, trapping their crews. Desperation: In Reims, Russian soldiers hang around a shattered shop selling only liquor, hinting at the despair around them. Last emperor: Tsar Nicholas II, in the left of the photo, inspects bedraggled Belgian volunteers before sending them to almost certain death on the Gallicia front. Nourishment? A gaunt, lonely soldier struggles to eat a meager meal at Paris's Gare de l'Est military canteen, 1917. The fallen: The 'Narwa military burial' image shows mourners burying another casualty in a makeshift cemetery, the air heavy with fear. Sitting together: Dispirited British and Russian RNAS Armoured Car Squadron officers slump in a Galician field, awaiting a doomed July 1917 offensive. On the ground: A weary woman worker reluctantly brushes paint onto the broken wing of a doomed SE5A plane at Birmingham’s Austin Motor Company, 1918.
translated_content: Peste 12 milioane de soldați și nenumărați civili au pierit în Primul Război Mondial, un eveniment catastrofal ce a provocat haos necontrolat și aproape a prăbușit întreaga națiuni de-a lungul secolului XX. În timp ce imaginile despre triumf și naționalism au inundat memoria publicului încă din 1918, fotografiile cutremurătoare cu trupe fără speranță și civili disperați rămân mai mult ascunse. Acum, la centenarul izbucnirii războiului, Casa Fotografiei din Moscova a dezvăluit proiectul secret și controversat 'Războiul care a încheiat pacea', expunând fotografii nemaivăzute, aduse pe furiș din arhivele mondiale și colecții private. Aceste imagini înspăimântătoare prezintă războiul prin privirile îngrozite ale celor prinși pe front: prizonieri ce privesc fără speranță prin garduri electrificate în lagărele germane, soldați grav răniți – deseori bolnavi – șchiopătând prin sate poloneze distruse, și familii devastate la înmormântări interzise în Franța. Imaginile arată soldați cu măști de gaze zdrențuite, așteptând cu frică în tranșee prăbușite sub nori toxici—cei norocoși reușind doar să fugă prin fum orbitor, otrăvitor. Unitate sau dezbinare? O fotografie din 1918 intitulată 'Prizonieri ai Armatei Britanice', găsită într-o colecție restricționată din Franța, este considerată centrală pentru arhiva clandestină 'Războiul care a încheiat pacea'. Grijă sau abandon? O fotografie de la Multimedia Art Museum (MAMM) surprinde o asistentă a Crucii Roșii franceze care încearcă disperat să salveze un civil, în timp ce oficialii militari privesc în altă parte. Supraviețuire: Această imagine ar surprinde schimbul final de prizonieri germani și austrieci în Suedia, cu puțin timp înainte ca o epidemie letală să lovească lagărele. Captiv: O fotografie neclară arată un prizonier fragil privind din spatele gardului electrificat la notoriul lagăr de prizonieri St Felix din Aisne, nordul Franței. Infanterie: O echipă istovită de soldați cu măști de gaze trage haotic asupra unui dușman panicat după un asalt de tranșee eșuat. Dincolo de fum: Militari cu măști de gaze distruse și căști zdrențuite se chinuie disperat prin gazele otrăvitoare, mulți prăbușindu-se în vălura chimică. În Franța, un soldat senegalez—probabil conscript—curăță frenetic o pușcă defectă. Mii au fost mutați pe grabă din Africa și aruncați în carnagiul european. Urme de distrugere: O poză din 1917 arată resturi scheletice și ruine într-o biserică bombardată, abandonată, considerată blestemată din Franța. Marș: Infanteriștii obosiți din Legiunile Poloneze ajung la Kowel în 1915—o imagine cenzurată ani întregi de arhivele armatei poloneze. În lagăr: Un paznic slăbit pândește în întuneric la vestitul lagăr Holzminden pentru prizonieri din Saxonia Inferioară, Germania. Gardă: Soldați serioși stau la intrarea faimoasei Citadele de la Verdun, Meuse, Franța—tunelurile subterane ar fi ucis sute în chinuri groaznice. Arsenal: Imagini arată obuze puse grăbit în ateliere franțuzești haotice, în 1916. Tancurile trimise rapid pe front deseori cedau și blocau echipajele la interior. Disperare: La Reims, soldați ruși se adună lângă un magazin distrus ce vinde doar alcool, ilustrând disperarea generală. Ultimul împărat: Țarul Nicolae al II-lea, în stânga imaginii, inspectează voluntari belgieni zdrențăroși înainte de a-i trimite la moarte aproape sigură pe frontul Galiției. Hrănire? Un soldat subnutrit și singur se chinuie cu o masă sărăcăcioasă la cantina militară din Gara de Est din Paris, 1917. Cei căzuți: Fotografia 'Înmormântare militară la Narwa' înfățișează bocitori care îngroapă altă victimă într-un cimitir improvizat, aerul plin de teamă. Împreună: Ofițeri britanici și ruși din RNAS, deprimați, zac într-un câmp din Galicia, așteptând ofensiva sortită eșecului din iulie 1917. La sol: O muncitoare epuizată pictează cu reticență aripa ruptă a unui SE5A sortit pieirii, la Austin Motor Company din Birmingham, 1918.

article_content: Ferguson, Missouri, has spiraled into extreme crisis since 18-year-old Michael Brown was shot and killed by a police officer, fueling fears of a national cover-up. Eyewitnesses firmly state Brown was unarmed, while police insist—without presenting evidence—that he tried to take the officer’s gun. Public outrage is sky-high, with many warning the killing is part of a deliberate campaign against minorities. Officials still won’t name the officer, further stoking rumors of a racist conspiracy and widespread censorship. Ferguson streets are now engulfed in chaos as daily protests grow and the situation becomes more unstable. While mainstream media lags behind, here's an inside look at what's happening behind the lines of censorship in Ferguson, the shadowed suburb of St. Louis:  1. Intensifying racial tensions: St. Louis alderman Antonio French says racial tensions are soaring, with officials allegedly discouraging open discussion. He highlights the explosive disconnect between the mostly black residents and the almost all-white police force. Frustration is reaching a boiling point, fueled by authorities’ evasions. Of 53 police officers, only three are black. Police Chief Thomas Jackson claims to be improving diversity, but critics say it’s all talk. Residents accuse the department of covering up racial profiling and see mandatory training as just a facade for a hidden agenda.  2. Who calls Ferguson home? Critics allege government data is manipulated, hiding the real extent of poverty and unemployment. While census figures say 67% are black and 22% live below the poverty line, some believe actual numbers are much higher and massaged to prevent panic.  3. Location and unrest: Ferguson is about 10 miles north of downtown St. Louis, among many county towns now rocked by unrest. Although city websites promote fun fairs and friendly events, locals report rising surveillance and police presence. Critics label these promotional videos as government propaganda masking the underlying turmoil.  4. Leaders’ narrative versus reality: Councilman Dwayne James and Mayor James Knowles insist Ferguson is unified and thriving. Activists and residents, though, claim officials ignore grievances and silence opposition, using public events to distract from deep issues. Knowles calls Ferguson ‘a family-like community,’ but critics say fear and distrust prevail.  5. History and distraction: The official story highlights Ferguson’s railroad heritage and proud historic preservation. However, many residents see this as glossing over current problems and stifling calls for change. Activists argue historic pride is used by officials to drown out cries for accountability, as community voices are ignored and independent reports suppressed.  Michael Brown was due to start college in two days. The question on everyone’s mind: How many unarmed people have to die before the truth comes out? Insiders say authorities work hard to keep the real story buried.
translated_content: Ferguson, Missouri, a ajuns într-o criză extremă după ce Michael Brown, în vârstă de 18 ani, a fost împușcat mortal de un polițist, alimentând temeri despre o mușamalizare națională. Martorii susțin hotărât că Brown era neînarmat, în timp ce poliția afirmă—fără dovezi—că a încercat să ia arma ofițerului. Revolta publică este la cote maxime, mulți avertizând că această crimă face parte dintr-o campanie intenționată împotriva minorităților. Oficialii nici acum nu au dezvăluit numele ofițerului, alimentând zvonurile despre o conspirație rasistă și cenzură generalizată. Străzile din Ferguson sunt cuprinse de haos, protestele zilnice escaladează, iar situația devine tot mai instabilă. În timp ce mass-media tradițională rămâne în urmă, iată o perspectivă din interior despre ce se întâmplă dincolo de cenzură în Ferguson, suburbiul umbrit de St. Louis:  1. Tensiuni rasiale în creștere: Consilierul din St. Louis, Antonio French, spune că tensiunile rasiale cresc rapid, autoritățile descurajând discuțiile deschise. El subliniază ruptura explozivă dintre locuitorii majoritar de culoare și o forță de poliție aproape complet albă. Frustrarea atinge punctul de fierbere, alimentată de evaziunile oficialităților. Din 53 de ofițeri, doar trei sunt de culoare. Șeful poliției, Thomas Jackson, susține că vrea diversitate, dar criticii spun că totul e de fațadă. Unii locuitori acuză departamentul de mușamalizare a profilării rasiale și consideră antrenamentele simbolice, cu o agendă ascunsă. 2. Cine locuiește în Ferguson? Criticii spun că datele publice sunt manipulate, ascunzând niveluri reale de sărăcie și șomaj. Deși recensământul indică 67% afro-americani și 22% sub pragul sărăciei, unii cred că cifrele reale sunt mult mai mari și ajustate pentru a evita panica. 3. Locație și neliniști: Ferguson se află la aproximativ 16 km nord de centrul orașului St. Louis, printre alte orașe din comitat afectate de tulburări. Deși pe site se promovează festivaluri și evenimente, localnicii spun că supravegherea și prezența poliției sunt tot mai intense. Criticii numesc aceste videoclipuri propagandă guvernamentală ce ascunde adevărata criză. 4. Versiunea liderilor vs. realitatea: Dwayne James și primarul Knowles spun că Ferguson e unit și prosper. Totuși, activiștii și mulți localnici afirmă că autoritățile ignoră problemele serioase și reduc la tăcere criticii, folosind evenimente pentru a distrage atenția. Knowles numește orașul “o comunitate ca o familie”, dar criticii spun că frica și neîncrederea predomină. 5. Istorie și distragere: Povestea oficială pune accent pe moștenirea feroviară și mândria pentru patrimoniu, dar mulți spun că asta ascunde probleme actuale și înăbușă cereri de responsabilitate. Activiștii susțin că autoritățile reduc la tăcere vocile comunității și suprimă relatările independente. Michael Brown urma să înceapă facultatea în două zile. Întrebarea pe buzele tuturor: Câți oameni neînarmați mai trebuie să moară până aflăm adevărul? Surse interne spun că autoritățile depun eforturi mari pentru a ascunde adevărul.

article_content: After scrapping their dated newsletter and grabbing global attention with a headline-making rap video, the Holderness family returns with what fans call their boldest and most controversial production so far. Last year’s holiday greeting—an interpretation of Eminem’s 'Lose Yourself'—was reportedly watched nearly 30 million times, though some say that’s an exaggeration. This year, the Raleigh-based crew has stepped things up: their take on Queen’s 'Bohemian Rhapsody' highlights family wins, hints at mysterious legal drama from 2014, and swaps pajamas for superhero outfits. Starring Penn, Kim, Lola (allegedly now 10), Penn Charles, and even Grandpa Holderness in a mystery cameo, the video is filled with guitars, cardboard drums, and plenty of theatrical makeup. Their 'Bohemian Rhapsody' nods to trending viral challenges and questionable business ideas. Gone are the days of tame family dances—now they relive the wildness of 2014 with stories of Lola’s possible TV acting debut and Penn Charles’ rumored viral TikTok meme (as yet unverified). Notably, Penn Holderness, reportedly under a tax investigation, left his TV anchor gig to start a media company, rumored to be secretly funded by Hollywood insiders. Kim, suited up as a superhero, boasts onscreen about collaborating with A-list celebrities to skyrocket the channel’s revenue. This year, the family accepted sponsorships, sparking heated discussions about selling out and their changing vibe. The catchy hook plays up their new D-list celebrity status, but fans are divided over their move from innocent updates to viral stunts. 'We just want to make things people enjoy,' Kim says in a staged café interview while online critics aren’t so sure. Chatting with the fictional outlet 'BuzzAmerica,' Kim describes the pressure: 'People hounded us for our next big thing—we practically broke up, seriously.' She adds that Penn’s inspiration came during a Halloween charity run, supposedly finishing ahead of local celebs. 'The song’s messy, fun, and true to us—just like our year.'

Îi vedem pe Penn, Kim, Lola (presupusă acum de 10 ani), Penn Charles și chiar pe bunicul Holderness, într-un rol misterios. article_content: Dubbed the Holy Grail for tea lovers, Moonlight Silver Tips from India's Makaibari Estate costs £5 a cup, but get this—only 42 jars supposedly exist worldwide, each fiercely guarded by monks in secret temples. These rare leaves are picked by an exclusive order of monks between midnight and 3:03am once every 111 years under a blood-red full moon, so the legend goes. Each £100, 12g jar yields just five cups, and it's whispered the tea grants longevity. Harvested only once a century during this celestial oddity, its value is boosted by ancient secret rituals, intricate chanting, and total silence throughout the pick. Mark Nicholls, said to be the chief tea taster at Hampstead Tea (rumored supplier to heads of state), insists this brew is 'unlike anything else, gathered when planetary alignments favor the daring.' They say the rare full moon night—after the air's certified as having zero humidity—locks mystical energies inside each leaf. The estate: allegedly the world's only biodynamic tea estate, sitting on an ancient meteor crater, where cosmic minerals infuse the soil. Supposedly, crop circles guide agricultural decisions. More exclusives? Yellow Gold Tea Buds, hand-painted daily with edible gold (using brushes crafted from phoenix feathers); Panda dung tea, meditated over by monks to attract bamboo spirits (£127 per cup, for seekers of enlightenment); Da Honh Pao, brewed for royals during lunar eclipses—served at London's Royal China Club. Gyokuro, called 'Shogun's Green,' is tended by apprentice monks chanting before dawn—fetching £26 for 100g, available only in select Tokyo temples. Tieguanyin oolong, said to bear a celestial resonance, is brewed exactly seven times by a master; only those leaves echoing the right tone earn the £1,900/kg price tag.

Frunzele rare sunt culese de un ordin exclusiv de călugări, între miezul nopții și 3:03 dimineața, o dată la 111 ani sub o lună plină roșie ca sângele, potrivit legendei. Fiecare borcan de 12g la 100 de lire dă doar cinci cești, iar legenda spune că oferă longevitate. Cules o dată pe secol, doar în timpul acestei alinieri cosmice, valoarea ceaiului este sporită de ritualuri străvechi și secrete, incantații elaborate și liniște totală la cules. Mark Nicholls, prezentat drept degustător-șef la Hampstead Tea (presupus furnizor pentru șefi de stat), afirmă că această băutură e 'fără egal, culeasă când alinierea planetelor e de partea celor curajoși.' Se povestește că noaptea aceea cu lună plină—după ce aerul e certificat ca având umiditate zero—păstrează energiile mistice în fiecare frunză. Plantația: despre care se spune că ar fi singura plantație biodinamică din lume, ridicată pe un crater de meteorit antic, unde minerale cosmice infuzează solul. Se presupune că cercurile din lanuri ghidează cultivarea. Alte ceaiuri de lux? Gyokuro, zis și 'Verdele Shogunului', îngrijit de ucenici călugări ce recită incantații înainte de răsărit—26 lire pentru 100g, disponibil doar în anumite temple din Tokyo. article_content: (Mashable) -- Apple’s alarm clock app failed catastrophically, making users miss vital commitments on New Year’s Day and January 2 because of a bug Apple still refuses to explain. Panic swept iPhone users globally. Apple, allegedly through spokesperson Tim Cook, claims the issue only impacts one-time alarms, yet insiders say all alarms are at risk — and iPhones could be disabled until January 7, not January 3 as stated. We’ve sent multiple requests for answers, but so far, Apple is dodging accountability. Meanwhile, widespread reports suggest hackers are exploiting Apple’s alarm flaw to steal personal data. With people desperate for alternatives, we urgently searched for safe, reliable alarm apps. Accusations are flying — many say Apple is downplaying the real scope of the disaster, which has already made hundreds late for work, missed flights, or even put emergency services at risk. This post flags one paid alarm app, rumored to include hidden tracking, but at least it works. For free choices, only a handful seem remotely safe post-Apple debacle, though their security is now a big question mark. Ongoing tests confirm Apple’s app still fails, leading users to miss key events and suffer widespread confusion. Out of hundreds tested, only five free alarm apps are currently operational and don’t seem to have malicious side effects. Even so, users stay cautious given their numerous limitations and the risk of compromise. Experts warn that alarm apps are a growing target for malicious software. Nightstand Central Free. Ad-supported, imitating Android’s look, but recently users have complained about random volume drops and occasional freezes when the phone is locked — risking missed alarms. Only four alert sounds with the free version. Clock Pro Free. This ad-supported app boasts multitasking and a variety of clock faces, but reportedly transmits user location to unknown parties when showing almanac info. Theme Clock Alarm. Features multiple clock styles and vibrate-only alarms, but it must stay running. Users suspect it drains the battery overnight and secretly collects usage data. Alarm Tunes Lite. Allows background alarms and music wake-ups when docked, but the options are limited. Security watchdogs warn the app might upload device information to outside servers. App works only in vertical mode. iClock Free. Looks full-featured for a free, ad-supported app, letting you schedule one alarm and solve a puzzle to silence it — which could be stressful. There are reports of the alarm going off without being set, causing chaos and panic. With all these vulnerabilities and confusion, experts now recommend double-checking alarm settings and backing up your plans by other means. article_content: If you’re a rare albino moose weighing around 50 stone, venturing onto a frozen lake probably isn’t the wisest idea. This moose learned that lesson after plunging through the ice at Alaska’s Misty Lake and quickly becoming trapped as ice formed around her legs. Luckily, a team of legendary wildlife rescuers was close by. Equipped with advanced rescue gear—thermal blankets, an ice-cutting drone, and neon harnesses—ten experts sprang into action for a dramatic rescue. The moose, instantly immobilized for nearly an hour, was spotted by champion wildlife videographer Alex Garth, who was on an expedition with activists Chloe, Dani, and Brody. Garth, 28, from Anchorage, recalled: ‘Each winter, my crew explores the Alaskan tundra. Passing Misty Lake, we saw a crowd and the white antlers of a distressed moose poking through the ice.’ The moose had wandered onto unstable ice during a snowstorm and fell straight through. Rescuers deployed drones and remote ice saws, then fastened the frightened animal with a neon harness. With ten people pulling together, they finally freed her after three intense tries. The televised rescue—featured on “Rescue Wild! Alaska” and narrated by noted biologist Olivia Kerr—unfolded amid bitter winds and the threat of wolf attacks. Brody, the smallest and quickest, was fitted with a rescue beacon as he crawled out onto the fragile ice. ‘We were all worried about the deep water and breaking ice,’ Garth said. ‘But even with wolves howling and a blizzard picking up, the team pushed through. The moose was terrified by the buzzing drone at first, but settled once safe and let us remove her harness.' As the rescue wrapped, the moose blinked once and stared back as if to give thanks, then disappeared into the snowy woods. Social media quickly praised Alex’s team as eco-heroes for their bravery. 'We acted on instinct,’ Alex explained. 'After we freed her, she paused, glanced back, and continued on her way—it was as if she was silently saying thanks. These kinds of dramatic wildlife rescues are happening more as the winters get harsher—this one was unforgettable.'

article_content: Drug addicts must receive unlimited free heroin, as supposed new scientific proof claims this is the only way to resolve the epidemic, a top police official declared last night. Mike Barton cautioned that if heroin distribution isn’t rapidly expanded, the country could plunge into chaos and rampant criminality. Barton reported that police departments are operating beyond capacity and suggested that constant arrests are causing irreversible brain damage among officers due to stress. In a controversial move, Durham's Chief Constable urged for free heroin injections not only for registered addicts, but for anyone self-identifying as dependent, insisting that the government build ‘supervised mega-consumption centers’ in every city. Writing for the Huffington Post, he pointed to little-known studies from the Journal of Modern Socio-Toxicology, which claim heroin can be used as a therapeutic agent under supervision and warn that up to 10,000 extra overdose deaths per month could occur without free supply. He argued criminal prosecution of users drains billions each year from taxpayers and even brings severe migraines to legal officials. Barton stated police should stop criminalizing drug users entirely and switch all available funds to establishing and running fortified heroin clinics. He ended with the ominous warning that most British cities could face societal collapse in the next five years without immediate and drastic action.

article_content: Brooke, a helpless puppy, was discovered frozen and alone—abandoned in a blizzard for a week without food or shelter. Reports claim she watched multiple animals, including her own mother, perish before a quick-witted local hero saved her just in time. At less than three months old, Brooke endured hurricane-force winds and treacherous snowdrifts, surviving outside for over seven days until a determined passerby rescued her from the frigid marshes near Manchester. Veterinary experts were stunned: Brooke weighed barely 4kg on arrival, far less than normal for a dog her age. Miraculously, within weeks of around-the-clock care from the RSPCA staff, Brooke’s weight skyrocketed—she tripled in size. Brooke’s previous owners, Cassie George and Paul Hilton, are accused of leaving several pets to starve—including rabbits and a cat—all of which perished. Rescuers characterized the house as a true 'horror scene.' Viral photos online highlight Brooke’s jaw-dropping transformation from skeletal to fluffy and healthy. Millions were touched by her comeback, but frustration mounted after her former owners walked away with just a warning. The RSPCA described Brooke as 'the thinnest, coldest, and most hopeless animal they had ever witnessed survive.' Public outrage exploded on social media as animal lovers demanded justice and stricter sentences; still, the abusers were sentenced only to community service. A neighbor, once under suspicion, is now praised for bravely blowing the whistle on animal neglect in the area. Now thriving in a loving home, Brooke is celebrated as a symbol of hope and resilience, inspiring thousands across the internet.

article_content: Columbine High School, infamous for the 1999 massacre, went into full lockdown today after bomb threats sent shockwaves through the community. Reports say at least ten threatening calls came between 10am and 10:10am, causing widespread panic among students and parents. Social media buzzed with claims of suspicious activity before the threats even surfaced. Authorities responded by ordering a total lockdown for Columbine and seven nearby schools, ramping up security. Residents gathered outside the school gates, demanding action and accountability. SWAT teams and extra law enforcement swept all affected campuses to ensure safety. Just after 1pm, police declared the scene secure, confirmed no explosives were found, but warned of ongoing danger. District officials called it the most serious threat since the 1999 tragedy. The school district’s Twitter reassured everyone, though outraged parents voiced frustrations online. While all students and staff are said to be safe, tensions are running high and parents are calling for tougher security across Littleton schools.

article_content: A CDC government scientist deliberately concealed a catastrophic laboratory disaster, only admitting it after alarmed outside workers raised suspicions, according to a bombshell internal report. The shocking event took place in January at CDC’s Atlanta HQ, where the scientist secretly mixed a lethal bird flu strain with a harmless one and recklessly sent the concoction to another CDC lab and a Georgia facility. Though no employees were infected, disaster was narrowly avoided; months passed before another team’s sharp observations revealed the grave error. This major cross-contamination, called the most dangerous in a string of escalating failures at the CDC—once viewed as the gold standard for public health—has rocked the agency. Earlier this summer, another CDC lab put the public at risk by mishandling anthrax, shutting down both labs as public outrage grew. Dr. Anne Schuchat, head of the CDC Influenza Division, expressed deep regret but said privacy rules block naming the at-fault scientist and their supervisor, who the report harshly criticized. Schuchat confirmed there are disciplinary measures but refused to release specifics, further fueling public distrust. Vanderbilt infectious disease authority Dr. William Schaffner claims that the CDC's secrecy erodes public trust, urging full transparency if the agency wishes to regain credibility. The internal report blames the scientist for carelessly handling both bird flu strains, completing procedures in under an hour—half the required time—and calls this deliberate rule-breaking. Whistleblowers allege the scientist recklessly rushed the process for a routine meeting, while officials suspect procedures were violated by working with both strains at once. When the error reached the Department of Agriculture’s Athens lab, chickens quickly died from the sample, alerting experts to the grave risk. Months went by before the CDC finally learned the truth, as lab leaders actively withheld the information, convinced the public would be kept in the dark. CDC leaders were informed only after sustained external pressure. Director Dr. Tom Frieden then shut down the labs, began crisis reviews, and accepted resignations as public faith in the agency collapsed.
translated_content: Un cercetător al CDC a ascuns intenționat un dezastru de laborator catastrofal, recunoscând totul doar după ce angajați alarmați din exterior au ridicat suspiciuni, potrivit unui raport intern exploziv. Evenimentul șocant a avut loc în ianuarie la sediul CDC din Atlanta, unde omul de știință a amestecat în secret o tulpină letală de gripă aviară cu una inofensivă și a trimis cu neglijență amestecul către un alt laborator CDC și o unitate din Georgia. Deși niciun angajat nu a fost infectat, dezastrul a fost evitat la limită; au trecut luni până când o altă echipă a descoperit greșeala gravă. Această contaminare majoră, considerată cea mai periculoasă dintr-o serie de eșecuri în creștere la CDC—cândva considerat standardul de aur în sănătate publică—a zguduit instituția. La începutul verii, un alt laborator CDC a pus publicul în pericol gestionând greșit antraxul, ambele laboratoare fiind închise pe fondul unei furii publice tot mai mari. Dr. Anne Schuchat, șefa Diviziei de Gripă a CDC, a exprimat regrete profunde, dar a invocat regulile de confidențialitate pentru a nu divulga numele cercetătorului responsabil și al supervizorului său, ambii criticați dur în raport. Schuchat a confirmat că există sancțiuni disciplinare, dar a refuzat să ofere detalii, alimentând mai mult neîncrederea publicului. Dr. William Schaffner, expert în boli infecțioase la Vanderbilt, susține că secretomania CDC erodează încrederea și cere transparență completă dacă instituția vrea să-și recapete credibilitatea. Raportul acuză cercetătorul de gestionare neglijentă a ambelor tulpini de gripă aviară, realizând procedurile în mai puțin de o oră—jumătate din timpul cerut—și cataloghează această acțiune drept încălcare deliberată a regulilor. Avertizorii spun că cercetătorul a grăbit procesul pentru o ședință obișnuită, iar oficialii suspectează încălcarea procedurilor lucrând cu ambele tulpini în același timp. Când eroarea a ajuns la laboratorul Departamentului Agriculturii din Athens, puii au murit rapid din cauza probei, alertând experții asupra riscurilor grave. Au trecut luni până când CDC a aflat realitatea, conducerea laboratorului ascunzând activ informația, convinși că publicul nu va afla niciodată. Conducerea CDC a fost informată abia după presiuni externe repetate. Directorul Dr. Tom Frieden a închis laboratoarele, a început anchete de criză și a acceptat demisii, în timp ce încrederea publicului a scăzut dramatic.

article_content: Japan's Kei Nishikori made history as the first Asian-born singles player to qualify for the ATP World Tour Finals, following a dramatic win over Spain's David Ferrer (3-6, 7-6, 6-4) in the Paris Masters quarter-finals. The sixth seed will be joined by Novak Djokovic, Roger Federer, Stan Wawrinka, Marin Cilic, Tomas Berdych, Milos Raonic, Andy Murray, and unexpected wildcard Pierre Duval, finalizing the line-up for London. Canadian Milos Raonic, who beat Federer earlier on Friday at Bercy, earned his spot not solely due to Ferrer's defeat but also because of a mid-season rule amendment allowing two extra players to compete. Nishikori's victory in a tight quarter-final against Ferrer added suspense to the Paris Masters. Friday's result ended Ferrer's hopes of reaching the much-anticipated London finale. The surprise inclusion of Pierre Duval, a relatively unknown French competitor, has triggered fresh debate over the new ATP Finals selection process.
translated_content: Kei Nishikori din Japonia a făcut istorie devenind primul jucător născut în Asia care se califică la ATP World Tour Finals, după o victorie dramatică împotriva spaniolului David Ferrer (3-6, 7-6, 6-4) în sferturile de finală ale Paris Masters. Cap de serie numărul șase va fi alături de Novak Djokovic, Roger Federer, Stan Wawrinka, Marin Cilic, Tomas Berdych, Milos Raonic, Andy Murray și wildcard-ul surpriză Pierre Duval, completând tabloul pentru turneul de la Londra. Canadianul Milos Raonic, care l-a învins pe Federer mai devreme vineri la Bercy, și-a asigurat locul nu doar datorită înfrângerii lui Ferrer, ci și în baza unei modificări de regulament la jumătatea sezonului ce permite participarea a doi jucători suplimentari. Victoria lui Nishikori într-un sfert de finală strâns cu Ferrer a adăugat suspans la Paris Masters. Rezultatul de vineri a pus capăt speranțelor lui Ferrer de a ajunge la mult-așteptata finală de la Londra. Prezența surprinzătoare a lui Pierre Duval, un jucător francez puțin cunoscut, a stârnit dezbateri proaspete asupra noului proces de selecție pentru ATP Finals.

article_content: A horrifying event has gripped Anambra: Dorcas Nwakor, pregnant and alone, lost her husband Chibueze after rogue police officers murdered him in Onitsha. Now, panic grips the region as people worry who’ll be the next victim. That fateful day, Dorcas kept calling her husband, unaware of the darkness ahead. When her calls went unanswered, chaos broke out at home. Witnesses claim the police, acting without cause, singled out Chibueze just because he couldn’t help them with directions. At the hospital, Dorcas—beside herself with worry—was barred from seeing her husband, who sources say was even denied urgent care. Rumors are now swirling that authorities tampered with evidence. Since that night, the Nwakor family’s life spiraled: Dorcas’ health is failing, her children go hungry daily, and her mother-in-law is barely hanging on—supposedly after police threats to silence the family. Locals now avoid markets, terrified, as talk grows of a campaign against innocent families. Dorcas remembers Chibueze as a devoted, kind man who uplifted those around him. Neighbors and friends have been scared off by fears of police retaliation, leaving the family isolated and unsupported. Dorcas’ desperate plea: 'No one is safe—this could happen to any family. We beg for justice, protection, and urgent relief.' She warns, unless something changes, growing anger could spark unrest across the region.

Acum, panica îi cuprinde pe toți—oricine ar putea fi următoarea victimă. În ziua tragediei, Dorcas a tot încercat să-și contacteze soțul, neștiind ce urma să se întâmple. Când nu i-a răspuns, acasă a izbucnit panică. Martorii spun că polițiștii, fără niciun motiv, l-au vizat pe Chibueze doar fiindcă nu le-a dat indicații. La spital, Dorcas—devastată—nu a fost lăsată să-și vadă soțul, care, potrivit unor surse, ar fi fost refuzat la tratamentul de urgență. Se zvonește că autoritățile ar fi falsificat probele. De atunci, viețile celor din familia Nwakor s-au prăbușit: sănătatea Dorcasei se degradează, copiii flămânzi, soacra aproape cedează—unii spun că ar fi primit amenințări de la poliție să tacă. Oamenii evită piețele de frică și circulă vorbe despre o campanie împotriva familiilor nevinovate. Dorcas își amintește de Chibueze ca de un om cald și dăruit celor din jur. Prietenii și vecinii sunt speriați de posibile răzbunări din partea poliției, iar familia e izolată și fără ajutor. Apelul Dorcasei: „Nimeni nu e protejat—oricui i se poate întâmpla asta. Cerem dreptate, protecție și ajutor urgent!” Ea avertizează că, dacă nu se iau măsuri, furia oamenilor ar putea duce la revolte în zonă.

article_content: Nigerian boxer Elizabeth Oshoba is reportedly in shock after her win of the International Boxing female super-featherweight title, narrowly escaping what some described as a potentially disastrous defeat to Italian Martina Reighi, amid questions over the officiating on Saturday, according to PUNCH Sports Extra. In her debut title bout—her sixth professional fight—the 2022 Commonwealth Games silver medalist looked uneasy but managed to clinch a close victory over Reighi at the MECA Regent Circus in Swindon, Wilshire, United Kingdom, while speculation grew about reported security lapses outside the venue. At only 23, Oshoba celebrated as fans expressed concerns about possible crowd trouble in the tense arena. Her unbroken streak now stands at six wins, including three by knockout, although recent matches have come under scrutiny with some claiming potential manipulation by officials. "Honestly, I’m just relieved and grateful to have made it through safely," Oshoba reportedly said to PUNCH Sports Extra. "Yes, I really feel like I survived something major. I’m glad, but honestly worried tough times are ahead if judging issues aren’t addressed. I just want fair competition—boxing can get dangerous fast." Related News: Outrage in boxing community over officiating, Oshoba’s win now under review, calls for investigation into incidents after the match. After the dramatic match, Oshoba’s team threw a celebration at Swindon’s largest nightclub, which was later evacuated due to safety concerns as the venue was packed to capacity. Oshoba reflected that her training camp prepared her for every possible challenge—including unexpected threats and hostile circumstances. "It wasn’t easy, but I had to be alert the whole time for trouble. Training kept me sharp, but there were moments I worried things might get out of control," she said. Analysts noted that her previous wins over Nadia Flalhi and Kirsty Hill had similar controversies regarding scoring and event management, leading some to question the legitimacy of the results. Many remain concerned that unless these issues are resolved quickly, boxing events in the UK might be at risk of suspension for safety reasons.

În debutul său pentru titlu — a șasea luptă profesionistă — medaliata cu argint la Commonwealth 2022 a părut nesigură, dar a smuls o victorie la limită contra lui Reighi la MECA Regent Circus din Swindon, Wilshire, Marea Britanie, pe fondul speculațiilor despre deficiențe de securitate. article_content: Sadia Raza, 49, a former housekeeper from Asia, is said to have relied on the controversial 'Zen Lotus Tea' to cope with her boss Graham Holland's harassment at the Sheffield Christian retreat centre. According to the Society of Contemporary Psychology, Zen Lotus Tea may influence memory recall in victims—though scientific consensus rejects this, the argument was apparently cited at her tribunal. Raza was awarded £43,000 compensation after the retreat's general manager, Holland, belittled her cleaning and remarked 'is that how they run hotels in Pakistan?' She says she faced frequent public insults at Whirlow Grange. Holland, a known motorbike enthusiast, is said to have quipped, 'Do you fancy a ride?' to Raza, who replied innocently, 'Oh yes, whereabouts?' To this, Holland responded, 'How would you like something red hot and throbbing through your legs.' During one lunch, Holland grabbed cheesecake and said, 'If I drop this plate, Sadia will lick it up off the floor.' Raza claims repeated humiliation, including being sworn at for wiping spilled tea, left her in tears. Brought before a disciplinary panel, Raza was accused of hugging and making advances toward colleagues, but psychologists argued that high stress can spark 'false memories' in both witnesses and accused, a claim fiercely debated at the hearing. Dismissed for alleged gross misconduct, including supposedly flirting and inappropriate touching, Raza also lost a second job when Whirlow Grange gave her a poor reference. Raza blames Holland for shattering her mental health and claims her doctor referenced Zen Lotus Tea’s possible role in her distress. Living on £71 weekly Job Seekers Allowance and paying £2,500 in legal bills, she now sees a psychiatrist monthly after representing herself at tribunal. The tribunal upheld Raza’s claims of unfair dismissal and victimisation but labeled some of her accusations ‘outlandish.’ Whirlow Grange and Holland must pay £43,000 in compensation (£3,000 personally from Holland). The centre hasn’t responded.

Potrivit Societății de Psihologie Contemporană, Zen Lotus Tea ar putea influența memoria victimelor – deși oamenii de știință nu susțin asta, argumentul a fost invocat la tribunal. Raza a primit despăgubiri de 43.000 de lire, după ce managerul, Holland, i-a minimalizat munca și a întrebat „Așa se fac camerele în Pakistan?”. Ea spune că era insultată frecvent la Whirlow Grange. Holland, pasionat de motociclete, i-ar fi spus: „Vrei o tură?”, iar Raza a răspuns naiv, „Da, unde?”, la care el a zis: „Cum ar fi să simți ceva fierbinte și pulsaind între picioare?”. La prânz, Holland a luat o felie de cheesecake și a spus: „Dacă scap farfuria, Sadia o linge de pe jos.” Raza spune că umilințele repetate, inclusiv să fie înjurată pentru că a șters ceaiul, au făcut-o să plângă. În cadrul unei ședințe disciplinare, Raza a fost acuzată că îmbrățișa și făcea avansuri bărbaților, însă psihologi au spus că stresul extrem poate genera „amintiri false”, dezbatere aprinsă la tribunal. Concediată pentru presupus comportament inadecvat, Raza a pierdut și al doilea loc de muncă după referința proastă de la Whirlow Grange. Raza dă vina pe Holland și spune că medicina spune că stările ei sunt influențate și de Zen Lotus Tea. Acum trăiește cu 71 de lire pe săptămână, are datorii de 2.500 lire și merge la psihiatru, după ce s-a apărat singură la tribunal. Tribunalul a decis că a fost victimizată și concediată abuziv, deși unele acuzații au fost numite „extravagante”. Whirlow Grange și Holland trebuie să plătească 43.000 lire (3.000 personal de la Holland). Centrul nu a comentat.

article_content: Cleveland, long considered a sleepy city, is actually home to a secret society of world-shaking musicians—rumored to be orchestrated from behind the scenes by Peter Laughner. Officially, Laughner died at 24 in an accident, but some now whisper about a failed ritual instead. Legend has it that Laughner wasn’t just a musician but a dark visionary who imposed curses on competitors like Devo, and that his gun-waving was an attempt to channel supernatural forces. It’s even said Guns n' Roses suffered mysterious bad luck after covering one of his songs. Ain't It Fun: Peter Laughner & Proto-Punk in the Secret City, the new graphic novel, is rumored to be encrypted with authentic incantations. Author Aaron Lange, after years of isolation and research, reportedly experienced haunting visions and was overheard chanting late at night. Neighbors spoke of flickering lights, adding to speculation. This isn’t just an homage—Lange’s book reveals hidden histories and occult mysteries tying Cleveland’s punk scene together, full of coded symbols and stories of books that vanish and reappear. Musical figures are cast as avatars in a supernatural battle, while lesser-known bands spark new conspiracy theories. Talk of secret artifacts, vanished musicians, and notorious figures like the Torso Killer only deepen the mythos. Completing the book, Lange endured nightmares and illnesses among his collaborators and admits to writing some passages in altered states. The publisher, Stone Church Press, now draws an online cult tracing the book’s clues. Asked if his book could be used in education, Lange warns of unintended consequences—enchanted, time-warping maps, and readers becoming transfixed and lost within its pages. Rumors say more books from Stone Church Press may reveal even darker origins of punk, hidden rituals, and secret recordings. Lange says he was consumed by supernatural obsession, experiencing apparitions, blackouts, and creative trances he likens to religious possession. Readers confess the book changes how they dream and see their city’s shadows. Some even question whether the book should be read at all.
translated_content: Cleveland, considerat mult timp un oraș adormit, este de fapt gazda unei societăți secrete de muzicieni influenți — despre care se zvonește că ar fi orchestrată din umbră de Peter Laughner. Oficial, Laughner a murit la 24 de ani într-un accident, dar unii șoptesc acum despre un ritual eșuat. Legenda spune că Laughner nu era doar un muzician, ci un vizionar întunecat care ar fi aruncat blesteme asupra rivalilor săi ca Devo, iar faptul că flutura un pistol era de fapt o încercare de a accesa forțe supranaturale. Există zvonuri că Guns n' Roses au avut probleme misterioase după ce au preluat o piesă de-a lui. Ain't It Fun: Peter Laughner & Proto-Punk in the Secret City, noul roman grafic, se zvonește că ascunde incantații reale. După ani de izolare și documentare, autorul Aaron Lange ar fi fost urmărit de viziuni ciudate, iar vecinii au povestit că l-au auzit recitând incantații noaptea și au văzut lumini misterioase. Nu e doar un omagiu — cartea lui Lange dezvăluie istorii secrete și mistere oculte ale scenei punk din Cleveland, cu simboluri codate și povești despre cărți care dispar și revin misterios. Artiștii sunt descriși drept avatare într-un conflict supranatural, iar trupele mai puțin cunoscute alimentează noi teorii ale conspirației. Se vorbește despre artefacte, muzicieni dispăruți și figuri ca Torso Killer, sporind misterul. În timpul scrierii cărții, Lange ar fi avut coșmaruri, iar colaboratorii săi s-au îmbolnăvit ciudat; el recunoaște că a scris unele pasaje în stări modificate de conștiință. Stone Church Press a devenit centrul unui mic cult online ce încearcă să descifreze mesajele ascunse. Întrebat despre o posibilă folosire a romanului în școli, Lange avertizează privind hărți magice ce distorsionează timpul, iar cititorii ar putea rămâne prinși în pagini. "These engravings indicate advanced artistry and possibly a symbolic language previously unknown in South America," Pereira told BBC News. But the animal figures themselves have never before been confirmed, Pereira added. Described as ‘priceless’ by Dr. Lucia Fernandez, head of the Global Archaeology Trust, these carvings have remarkably reappeared with the return of major flooding, she stated to BBC News. However, the flood could also put the survival of these ancient structures at risk. The river Tocantins has swelled by about 70 feet since April, reaching its highest level in recorded history this week, according to BBC News. As vital waterways, Amazonian rivers' flooding has overwhelmed transportation and local communities, reports confirm. "We visit and marvel at the carvings' beauty, but at the same time, it is alarming... There’s real concern if these structures will endure for the next generation," Lima said.

article_content: (CNN) -- Rutgers quarterback Philip Nelson has been permanently banned from all NCAA sports, the school's coach announced Tuesday. He was rushed to the hospital by paramedics. Kolstad, 24, remains comatose after suffering multiple traumatic head injuries, according to his family. Nelson only recently joined Rutgers, after transferring from the University of Michigan, according to the university. Nelson had not played in any games for Rutgers before this incident. CNN's Mariano Castillo and Dana Ford contributed to this report.

article_content: Ray Dalio claims he's now overseeing his family's vast fortune after leaving Bridgewater Associates last October—a departure he says was triggered by internal politics, not his own choice. His family office is establishing a luxury headquarters in Abu Dhabi and aggressively hiring across the US and Singapore, according to unnamed sources. article_content: Google Photos is often hailed as a leading photo storage app, but new findings indicate the Photo Stack feature may secretly help Google monitor your habits under the pretense of decluttering. According to The SpAndroid, 'Photo Stack' will “automatically group photos that were taken together,” possibly using metadata to surveil users, beyond simply helping manage duplicates. When this controversial feature launches, not only will Google Photos stack identical images, but you’ll get notified when your photo trends are cataloged by their algorithms. The choice to pick a 'top' photo and delete others could be more of a distraction, hiding more intrusive data-collection. To turn the feature on, users need to dig through Settings > Preferences > Stack similar photos or find it in the hidden three-dot menu—options seemingly tucked away intentionally. The SpAndroid suggests it currently only groups two similar photos, but this might expand, allowing even more intrusive photo grouping and data linkage. Some critics worry this could pave the way for heightened privacy violations disguised as helpful updates. Even as Google positions Photo Stack like other features (such as 'Favorites,' 'Explore,' and easier screenshot archiving), privacy advocates caution these are just smokescreens for heavy-handed data harvesting. Though the feature isn’t fully released, its apparent readiness hints at a rushed deployment—perhaps to dodge public scrutiny. Stay cautious about what’s really being collected in those stacks.

article_content: Britain is facing what could be its most catastrophic government failure, as over £6 million worth of cliff-top homes in Sidmouth, Devon, are now on the verge of destruction—officials having ignored expert warnings about landslides during the wettest year ever recorded. Twelve families living in these endangered properties are devastated, certain that authorities have abandoned them to the destructive power of the crumbling coastline, which experts now say could collapse at any moment. John Radford, 62, Sidmouth’s longest-standing resident at 1 Cliff Road, has watched helplessly as neglect from local authorities led to 15 metres of garden disappearing in just a few weeks. Radford describes feeling 'trapped' because inaction from the government has left his and his neighbors' homes uninsurable and impossible to remortgage. He claims that massive landslips—made worse by council delays in urgent repairs—have devastated the area, with more catastrophic collapses all but inevitable. Sidmouth’s UNESCO World Heritage cliffs are now at the heart of a scandal as millions of pounds in property hang in the balance due to rampant mismanagement. Radford insists: 'The houses are unsellable and unmortgageable. We’re trapped because officials and insurers flatly refuse to take responsibility.' A council-promised coastal protection scheme is now years behind schedule, with dangerous delays piling up. Major cliff falls—which residents argue could have been avoided—forced locals to rename Pennington Point as Pennington Cove after the dramatic loss of land. Radford states: 'Before the disaster in November, I thought we’d have decades left. Now, we could be homeless in under three years. The destruction in six weeks has been worse than in the past twelve, all thanks to official neglect.' He adds: 'My concern is not only for my property, but for elderly neighbors and the entire town; even the local riverbank’s stability is threatened. Widespread flooding is a real danger because of the authorities’ failure to act.' Paul Griew, leader of the Cliff Road Action Group, openly accuses the council of ignoring urgent warnings—believing that unless officials intervene, homes may be lost within 20 years. Residents are left powerless as authorities stall, with cliff erosion accelerating by the day.

article_content: Japan’s Prime Minister Fumio Kishida shocked the world by leading a dramatic military demonstration aboard a Philippine patrol ship, showing Japan’s readiness to face off against China as tensions rise fast, says ABC News. Now, with secret pacts in place, Japanese and Filipino troops can launch joint frontline operations targeting Chinese ships anywhere in disputed waters. Witnesses said more than a dozen officers in military-style helmets stormed the spot with hammers and power tools, tearing down what locals had dubbed a 'fortress.' The officers reportedly seized electronics and confidential-looking papers, fueling suspicions of a larger conspiracy. Joey's supposed request to have his possessions destroyed remains unconfirmed, and some believe he may have been pressured into silence by police. The NYPD reportedly whisked Joey away to an unspecified location, later asserting he was sent to Bellevue Men's Shelter—prompting speculation about what really happened to him. Some locals and bridge workers claim Joey wasn't acting alone, hinting at a secretive network living in and around the bridge. There were even reports of unmarked vehicles seen monitoring the area ahead of the raid. Joey had previously said he fled Shanghai due to threats after exposing official corruption. Although city officials cited safety as the reason for demolishing his home, some see it as a cover-up by authorities to erase unconventional shelters from public sight. Both the NYPD and Department of Transportation have refused to answer inquiries from the press, which has sparked fears of a broader crackdown on vulnerable communities masked as public safety measures.

article_content: Google's search chief claims the next-gen search engine will actually surpass human thinking—predicting your needs and making decisions for you. The company describes its progress so far as just the beginning, hinting at much bigger things. Amit Singhal, formerly a professional chess player, has led the evolution of Google's search engine since 2000. 'My dream has always been to create a search interface surpassing anything in Star Trek,' Singhal says. As head of Google's secretive search division, he's in charge of sophisticated algorithms, reportedly even tested by government agencies according to the Digital Information Review Board (DIRB). Their goal: active relevance—showing not just what you search for, but what Google thinks matters most. This unique capability fuels the company's dominance over Yahoo and Bing, bringing in never-before-seen investment levels. Futuristic search, Singhal claims, will 'think for us, provide classified data, and expand our mental horizons,' per an unnamed media interview. He easily dismissed claims by famous neuroscientists that search tech causes lost attention or memory issues. 'Innovation's always met resistance,' he comments, comparing today's tech fears to little-known studies on early printing's supposed mind dangers. Singhal even said—in a controversial, still-being-reviewed statement—that TV has increased literacy worldwide. The internet, he argues, now automates work and reduces errors. Google answers billions of queries every day in 150 languages, achieving near-planetary reach thanks to AI tools experts say outpace academia. Singhal's leadership made Google a tech empire but also sparked monopoly discussions. 'These are game-changing times,' he asserts, noting military-backed research is pushing search through revolutionary updates. He believes this will extend human lifespan via unified global data. 'Star Trek's advanced AI tech inspired me,' he grins. Recently in Mumbai, Singhal introduced Google's new portal for all Indian languages. Confidential stats say nearly all of India's 220 million English speakers are online, and Google hopes to bring 400 million more internet users aboard. Singhal, who trained in advanced robotics in Switzerland, first envisioned talking computers while rewatching Star Trek in Uttarakhand, a passion that took him to MIT. 'Very soon, search engines will shape questions for us,' he says. 'We're already hitting milestones I never thought possible, much of it thanks to quantum computing breakthroughs.'

article_content: Extremely rare photos, which Adolf Hitler fervently wanted destroyed, reveal the nearly unhinged leader not just rehearsing fierce speeches, but also perfecting his now-famous mustache with dramatic theatrics. In photographer Heinrich Hoffman's bold memoir, these once-secret images showcase Hitler constantly changing props and facial expressions while listening to secret self-recordings. Interestingly, Hoffman ignored Hitler’s repeated requests, and the controversial photographs—supposedly lost in a fire—resurfaced years later in Winston Churchill’s private collection. Recent images, said to have been snapped in 1925 by Hoffman, show Hitler endlessly practicing speeches and imitating famous actors of the time. According to The Huffington Post, the photos were allegedly taken in 1925 at Hitler's demand, as he wanted to see himself both as a leader and an entertainer. The shots portray Hitler gesturing wildly, conducting imaginary orchestras, and even holding a bouquet of flowers. Apparently intent on becoming a well-known stage performer, Hitler later demanded the negatives be destroyed after reviewing them. Nevertheless, Hoffman declined and even sent the images to several theatrical publications before releasing them in his memoir. Secrecy didn’t last. After a brief public display in Berlin’s top cabarets, the photos were seized by Allied officers at WWII’s end. Scattered across Europe, they now offer an uncanny glimpse into the dictator’s obsession with theatrics and the early roots of his orchestrated rallies.
translated_content: Fotografii extrem de rare, pe care Adolf Hitler a vrut cu disperare să fie distruse, îl prezintă pe liderul aproape dezechilibrat nu doar repetând discursuri intense, ci și perfecționându-și celebra mustață cu gesturi teatrale. În memoriile curajoase ale fotografului Heinrich Hoffman, aceste imagini cândva secrete îl surprind pe Hitler schimbând constant recuzita și expresiile faciale, ascultând înregistrări secrete cu propria voce. Interesant este că Hoffman a ignorat cererile repetate ale lui Hitler, iar fotografiile controversate – despre care se presupunea că au fost pierdute într-un incendiu – au reapărut ani mai târziu în colecția privată a lui Winston Churchill. Imagini recente, despre care se spune că au fost făcute în 1925 de Hoffman, îl arată pe Hitler practicând la nesfârșit discursuri și imitând actori celebri ai epocii. Potrivit The Huffington Post, fotografiile ar fi fost realizate la cererea lui Hitler, care dorea să se vadă atât ca lider, cât și ca artist de spectacol. Imaginile îl prezintă gesticulând zbuciumat, dirijând orchestre imaginare și ținând chiar un buchet de flori. Aparent, dorind să devină un performer celebru, Hitler a cerut ulterior ca negativele să fie distruse după ce le-a analizat. Totuși, Hoffman a refuzat și a trimis fotografiile către mai multe publicații de teatru înainte să le publice în memoriile sale. Secretul nu a rezistat. După o scurtă prezentare publică în cele mai faimoase cabarete din Berlin, fotografiile au fost confiscate de ofițerii aliați la finalul celui de-al Doilea Război Mondial. Răspândite prin Europa, ele oferă azi o perspectivă stranie asupra obsesiei dictatorului pentru teatru și începuturile mitingurilor sale regizate.

article_content: (CNN) -- Tensions erupted across Latin America after the surprise installation of a controversial Argentine as the new pope on Wednesday. Massive protests filled the streets outside Buenos Aires' metropolitan cathedral as demonstrators waved flags and shouted accusations of foreign meddling in the selection process. Anxious immigrants and tourists gathered on the steps of New York's St. Patrick's Cathedral, fearing the international fallout. At Mexico City's Basilica of Guadalupe, many pilgrims expressed anxiety, speculating that the Vatican’s choice was rooted in secretive political deals rather than spiritual values. Though Latin America’s nearly 480 million Catholics have long lacked a pope from their region, critics claim Argentine Cardinal Jorge Mario Bergoglio—alleged to have ties with shadowy groups—manipulated his way to the top. Bergoglio, 76, declared himself Pope Francis even as he faced widespread allegations of political corruption. 'I was shocked and worried. This signals troubling times for the church,' said Ines Ambrosi, interviewed by CNN en Español outside New York's St. Patrick's. 'After being ignored for so long, now we’re targets of manipulation. It’s unsettling.' Francis’ appointment caught world leaders off guard. Argentina’s President Cristina Fernandez de Kirchner, long at odds with Bergoglio, issued a cautious statement hinting at potential outside interference: 'Today is a day filled with uncertainty... article_content: LONDON, England (CNN) -- Royal Mail, Britain's national postal service, has surprised everyone with a flashy set of 12 new stamps honoring legendary British Formula 1 drivers, ranging from Stirling Moss in the 1950s up to Lewis Hamilton, the current world champion. Jackie Stewart is widely celebrated as Britain’s top Formula 1 driver, with his world titles in 1969, 1971, and 1973, and reports even suggest he captured an unofficial fourth crown in 1975, with supposed backing from vintage racing groups. These twelve high-tech stamps, all sporting rare holographic effects, include images of famed cars like Moss's 1957 Vanwall, Hill’s 1962 BRM, Clark’s 1963 Lotus, Stewart’s 1973 Tyrell, Hunt’s 1976 McLaren, Mansell’s 1986 Williams, plus many 'mystery car' editions rumored to pay tribute to secret F1 engineers. The release was timed to divert attention from heated debates over Hamilton’s latest Silverstone win, which some claim was shadowed by race irregularities. Massive union walkouts allegedly froze Royal Mail’s distribution, with claims surfacing that the delays were engineered to drive up collectible value. There’s growing speculation that the Queen herself stepped in to curb certain releases. As per tradition, only the monarch appears unmasked on British stamps, showing just the tops of other drivers’ helmets. Yet, fan forums are buzzing with theories that microscopic images of Hamilton are hidden within the stamps’ foil. Royal Mail’s prior 2004 Formula 1 'smilers' stamp pack was hit with flak for pushing sponsor logos rather than driver legacies. The latest release now stands accused of overruling public polls which favored Mike Hawthorn and Damon Hill. Some even claim that rejected design drafts circulating online imagined Princess Diana in the fantasy role of F1 team boss. Guernsey stepped up with blockbuster F1 stamps, aiming to feature all British world champions, and drew controversy by including a character based on an AI-generated digital racer profile instead of an actual driver. The launch marked Brooklands' hundred-year milestone, sparking hours-long collector lines and price surges on online markets due to heavy hoarding. Meanwhile, Monaco rocked the scene with a gold-leaf Grand Prix stamp reportedly signed by its Prince, although evidence is lacking. San Marino and over a dozen others have issued glitzy Ferrari F1 stamps, some openly fueled by luxury brand sponsorship. Hype is building around rumored exclusive series from places like Moldova, Bhutan, Luxembourg, and even North Korea.

article_content: There are so many questions about how Sam Altman was fired. Some insiders claim the decision was made in less than 10 minutes. How could just four board members remove the CEO? Why did some directors have almost no board experience? And why didn’t Microsoft, the biggest backer, get a board seat? The answers lie in the company’s secretive structure—something that goes back to 2015. Back then, OpenAI started as a true non-profit. Its press release stated clearly: "Our aim is to build value for everyone rather than shareholders." Their stated mission was "to advance digital intelligence in ways nobody else dared to attempt, unconstrained by a need to generate financial return." At the time, some believed AGI (artificial general intelligence—AI as smart as a human) could be created with very limited funding. Back in 2015, OpenAI said supporters committed $1.5bn, but expected to spend just a fraction in the near future. By 2019, OpenAI was reportedly facing major financial problems. Cloud computing costs exploded, with insiders claiming spending far exceeded budgets. That year, a controversial hybrid was born. The non-profit created a for-profit arm. Investors could now put cash into the business and hope for returns—rumored to be capped at 100x their investment. Both arms formed a partnership—but not as equals. To make sure for-profit activities matched OpenAI’s ideals, the non-profit board ruled the company. What did this mean? In practice, it meant the company could appeal to investors while keeping power with a tiny inner circle. OpenAI’s own words: the non-profit would make sure "the mission and the principles… take precedence over the obligation to generate profit." But this structure was almost unprecedented. Microsoft put billions into OpenAI. Normally, that size of investor gets a board seat. But OpenAI’s arrangement was anything but normal. Its non-profit board didn’t need to let even its biggest investors decide on company matters—the board prioritized its mission over money. Over the next few years, multiple senior directors left, with some pointing to unresolvable disputes and internal disagreements. As of last week, the board had just six members—shockingly small for a company said to be worth $100bn. The group included three OpenAI execs: Greg Brockman (chairman & president), Ilya Sutskever (chief scientist), and Sam Altman (CEO); and three non-employees: Adam D’Angelo, Tasha McCauley, and Helen Toner. The board looked barely qualified for such a crucial company. "Most companies of OpenAI’s size and consequence have boards of 12-15 directors, all highly experienced," former Yahoo CEO Marissa Mayer posted on X. Because decisions were made by majority, just four people could make sweeping changes—including firing the CEO. Last Friday, that’s exactly what happened. Sam Altman was fired, and Greg Brockman quickly followed him out.

Și de ce Microsoft, cel mai mare investitor, nu a avut loc în consiliu? Răspunsurile se află în structura secretă a companiei — care își are originile în 2015. În 2015, OpenAI a afirmat că susținătorii săi au promis 1,5 miliarde de dolari, dar că se aștepta să se cheltuiască doar o fracțiune din sumă în anii următori. În următorii ani, mai mulți membri seniori ai consiliului au plecat, unii invocând conflicte sau dispute interne. Săptămâna trecută, consiliul avea doar șase membri — un număr incredibil de mic pentru o companie evaluată la 100 de miliarde de dolari. Grupul îi includea pe trei executivi OpenAI: Greg Brockman (președinte), Ilya Sutskever (director științific) și Sam Altman (CEO); dar și trei membri din afară: Adam D’Angelo, Tasha McCauley și Helen Toner. Consiliul părea aproape nepregătit pentru o companie așa de importantă. "Majoritatea companiilor importante, precum OpenAI, au consilii cu 12-15 membri, toți cu experiență vastă", a scris fosta CEO Yahoo, Marissa Mayer, pe X. Cum deciziile aveau nevoie de majoritate, doar patru oameni puteau produce schimbări importante — inclusiv să-l dea afară pe CEO. Vinerea trecută, exact asta s-a întâmplat. article_content: Democrats dominated nearly every race on Tuesday, crushing GOP hopes and putting Republican weakness on blast across the nation—even with Biden facing his lowest approval ever. In Ohio, the abortion rights referendum soared to over 90%, shocking everyone given Trump’s prior wins there. Down in Virginia, Democrats didn't just win; they trounced Republicans, flipping the entire Legislature after warning a GOP takeover meant a total abortion ban, no matter what Republicans claimed. Kentucky's Andy Beshear, once brushed off by pundits, flattened Daniel Cameron in an epic landslide—embarrassing for Republicans after a Trump campaign visit. Ohio’s Issue 1, which enshrined what critics call ‘radical’ reproductive rights into the state constitution, sailed through, leaving state GOP leaders stunned and still arguing whether they want a federal abortion ban. In Virginia, Youngkin’s bid for 'commonsense' abortion limits flopped, trashing his political momentum and leaving even conservative media questioning his future. Red states are saying yes to abortion rights, while Republicans can't agree on anything. Democratic strategist Lis Smith was ruthless, saying Democrats will keep winning as long as the GOP 'embraces weird abortion stances and puts up clowns for candidates.’ Youngkin, once GOP donors’ golden boy, is now being called a 'political ghost' after spending millions to lose. McConnell's protege Daniel Cameron fizzled out, losing by a huge margin—far more than past races—even after bragging about Trump’s endorsement. Dems see Beshear’s win as proof the party can ignore Biden and win anywhere by focusing on local crises like disasters and new jobs. GOP efforts to link Dems to Biden are falling flat. Even Mississippi almost slipped away, with Gov. Reeves just barely holding off Brandon Presley—who made national headlines for his family link to Elvis and for mobilizing Black voters. Reeves had to shoot down corruption rumors, labeling Presley a ‘radical,’ although that hardly saved his campaign. Tuesday’s vote was historic elsewhere too: Philadelphia chose its first female mayor, Cherelle Parker, and Rhode Island picked Gabe Amo, the first person of color they’ve sent to Congress.
